title: First Light for SPECULOOS Southern Observatory’s Callisto Telescope
caption: The Horsehead Nebula, imaged by the Callisto telescope of the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The famous Horsehead Nebula appears in the very first image taken by Callisto, one of the telescopes of the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory. A first light is the first image a newly commissioned telescope takes, and well-known objects like this are often chosen to mark the occasion.
The Horsehead is a dark nebula, a thick cloud of dust that blocks the light from behind it, so it shows up as a silhouette.

SPECULOOS has a different main job. It is made up of four 1-meter telescopes built to hunt for planets, and they are named after Jupiter's Galilean moons, of which Callisto is one. The observatory will look for planets the size of Earth around nearby brown dwarfs and ultra-cool stars. The telescopes sit at ESO's Paranal Observatory in Chile's Atacama Desert, near the Very Large Telescope and VISTA.

understand.summary: The Callisto telescope took this image through visible and near-infrared filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The Horsehead is too faint to see with the naked eye. A camera exposure gathers enough light to reveal its outline.
